content:
I’m a Product Manager with a software engineering background. At TransPerfect I own the backlog and roadmap for GlobalLink Enterprise, an enterprise B2B localization and automation platform: prioritizing features, coordinating delivery with engineering, and writing the technical documentation for the product and its API.
Before moving into product, I spent several years as a developer, building web and mobile products end to end, often as the person defining the requirements as well as writing the code. That lets me work closely with engineers, reason about APIs and technical trade-offs, and write specs that are ready to build.
I’m most interested in technical and platform products, fintech and crypto, B2B SaaS and workflow automation, and games. I’m open to on-site, hybrid and remote roles, and comfortable working with async-first teams.
Outside work, I’m part of a weekly Dungeons & Dragons group, and I write some of our adventures myself.

content:
AlejoRamirezGismondi/SpringLightC# 30As part of my Software Engineering degree, I was required to complete a final thesis. I centered mine around the concept of Game Development, investigating and presenting a 200 page paper on the subject. Complementary to this, I put the researched knowledge into practice by actually developing my own simple videogame in the Unity Engine.
This game features different mechanics inspired in other similar RPGs, farm-simulator games and other puzzle games. The pixel art presented in the game is either from open source, royalty-free sources or created by myself in Aseprite.
The project took about six months to be completed, between Art, Coding and Game Design. This was my first videogame ever created so I had to learn how to do things from scratch and iterate over them as I discovered new and better solutions. I also borrowed the help of friends and family to carry out playtests and refine features.
You can find both the original paper and the presentation in the following links. All material is published under the Apache License 2.0.
